architecture_atoms_ingested.design_consequence: KEEP deterministic durable workpackage/capsule semantics; ADAPT_TO_GRID by adding an explicit execution-binding bridge between workpackage and actual child lifecycle.
REPAIR. Child lifecycle and actor identity must not collapse to parent/session bookkeeping.

architecture_delta.before: The donor has durable workpackage/handoff state and generic hook telemetry, but no verified binding from a workpackage to the exact native child actor and its per-tool invocations.
architecture_delta.after: Frankenstein 2.0 now requires a first-class WorkExecutionBinding layer: durable work identity stays in UnifiedDB/GRID, while native runtime actor identity and per-invocation identity are captured as evidence. workpackage_id expresses delegated intent/work; agent_id identifies the native child actor when observed; tool_use_id identifies one concrete tool invocation. session_id remains context, not sufficient actor/invocation identity.
frankenstein_2_action: Preserve deterministic handoff/workpackage creation as the canonical delegated-work intent surface.

Add explicit lifecycle capture for the actual spawn mechanism; prefer native Claude child identity if the installed runtime proves the documented ABI, otherwise use a bounded wrapper with equivalent exact identity.
Persist workpackage_id↔agent_id binding at child start and child terminal state; preserve resume/replacement transitions rather than overwriting identity history.
Bind every child tool call by tool_use_id and actor identity so overlapping calls cannot cross-wire effect/completion evidence.

Do not use SubagentStart as an enforcement gate because official semantics say it cannot block child creation; admission belongs before spawn/Agent invocation and mutating effects remain gated at deterministic pre-side-effect boundaries.
Treat worktree isolation as an optional containment primitive only after target-host verification; it does not itself grant effect authority.
Feed completion back through typed receipts bound to workpackage+actor+invocation+source/runtime identity; textual completion claims remain non-authoritative.
